**Description**
AWS Security’s Security Communications (SecComms) team builds and operates the platforms, tools, and systems that enable Amazon’s security organization to communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders at scale. We support security events, ongoing security programs, vulnerability communications, and strategic initiatives that span multiple Amazon business units and AWS services. Our engineering products are the connective tissue between security findings, remediation owners, and the people responsible for keeping Amazon and its customers safe.
  
  
We are seeking an experienced Software Development Engineer to drive the design, development, and operation of software systems that power security communications workflows, automation, and integrations at scale. This role is for a builder who brings engineering rigor to ambiguous problems, cares deeply about customer outcomes, and thrives working across organizational boundaries with security engineers, program managers, and communications professionals.
  
  
Security Communications serves as the engineering and operations hub for AWS-related security messaging, stakeholder notification, and communications tooling across the organization. Our team is responsible for building scalable platforms that enable consistent, reliable, and timely communication during high-severity security events, coordinated vulnerability disclosure, and routine security program operations. We are a cross-functional team — engineers work shoulder-to-shoulder with communications professionals, security operations personnel, AWS service owners, and executives. Candidates should be comfortable collaborating in this environment and contributing to discussions that span both technical and non-technical domains.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
Design & Delivery
  
  

* Design and deliver software features and improvements spanning the full lifecycle — including scoping, architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance — for major portions of the SecComms platform.
* Work backwards from customer and stakeholder needs to define requirements and translate them into well-designed, maintainable software solutions.
* Design cohesive software implementations for difficult problems with visible risks or roadblocks; bring clarity to ambiguous requirements and identify simple, extensible designs.
* Balance constraints across new feature development, technical debt, and operational reliability; limit short-term workarounds in favor of sustainable solutions.
* Produce high-quality, well-tested, documented code that adheres to the Amazon Code Bar and can be maintained and extended by teammates who did not author it.

Operational Excellence
  
  

* Demonstrate operational excellence in all work; own and operate production services with appropriate alarms, telemetry, runbooks, and on-call response.
* Actively participate in operational support; identify and resolve the root causes of operational issues rather than accepting the status quo.
* Routinely identify and execute on opportunities to improve team operational processes, automation, and tooling — do not settle for operational friction when it can be eliminated.
* Ensure that software failures are addressed with permanent fixes; avoid recurring incidents by addressing systemic causes.

Collaboration & Cross-Functional Partnership
  
  

* Work closely with security engineers, program managers, communications leads, and partner teams to understand the business and customer value of your software.
* Operate effectively across team and organizational boundaries; collaborate with adjacent teams in an inclusive and constructive manner when integrations, dependencies, or shared priorities arise.
* Balance customer requirements with team requirements; make effective priority tradeoffs between feature development and operational work.
* Communicate clearly and proactively about work in progress, technical decisions, blockers, and scope changes to all relevant stakeholders — both technical and non-technical.

**Company Overview**
Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.
  
  
The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models.
  
  
**Operating Principles:**
Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:
  
  

* Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.
* Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.
* Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.
* Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.
  
  
****AI-First by Default****
We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.
  
  
That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:
  
  

* Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.
* Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.
* Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.
* Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.
  
  
**About The Role**
Deepgram's speech models are among the fastest and most accurate in the world, and we have deep machinery for running them on NVIDIA GPUs. Our customers need them on everything else: non-NVIDIA accelerators, embedded SoCs, mobile application processors, DSPs and NPUs, and purpose-built devices with tight memory, compute, thermal, and power budgets. When a target platform's standard kernels and runtime can't run a Deepgram model well enough, someone has to go below them. That is this role.
  
  
As an
**Embedded AI Engineer**
on the Partner Platform Engineering team, you work at the lowest layer of our edge stack. You write and optimize custom kernels and operators for specific hardware, collapse models onto device-specific execution units, and do the target-side quantization and assembly-level tuning that standard toolchains can't. You hand what you build up to Applied ML Engineers, who fit Deepgram models to your kernels. Your work is what makes a new hardware platform viable for Deepgram at all.
  
  
This role is a great fit for a senior embedded engineer who has spent their career close to the metal and wants to point that at speech AI, or a staff-level engineer who wants to define how Deepgram's models get onto new silicon. We'll set the level to your experience.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Write and optimize custom kernels and operators (C, C++, Rust, and platform assembly or intrinsics) for non-NVIDIA accelerators, embedded SoCs, DSPs, and NPUs where the vendor's standard operator set is insufficient for Deepgram models.
* Own target-side optimization: collapse models onto device execution units through quantization, operator fusion, memory layout, and architecture-specific compilation to meet latency, memory, power, and thermal budgets.
* Integrate with vendor NPU/DSP toolchains and edge inference runtimes, and extend them with custom operators when the graph doesn't map cleanly.
* Deliver kernels and runtime components as reusable building blocks that Applied ML Engineers can target when adapting models, with clear interfaces and documented constraints.
* Build performance-critical runtime code for embedded environments, including embedded Linux, bare-metal, and RTOS targets.
* Establish per-platform benchmarking and validation for latency, accuracy, power, memory footprint, and utilization, and catch regressions before they ship.
* Partner with silicon and platform vendors on SDK integration and low-level performance tuning for new chipsets and reference platforms.
* Feed hardware constraints back to Applied ML and Research so model designs are easier to land on constrained targets.

**You'll Love This Role If You**

* Find deep satisfaction in making a large model run on hardware that was never meant to run it, and still hitting accuracy and latency targets.
* Reach for the profiler and the ISA manual before you reach for a bigger chip.
* Would rather write the kernel than wait for the vendor to ship it.
* Care about the details that don't show up in a cloud benchmark: cold start, power draw, thermals, memory fragmentation, cache behavior.
* Prefer hard, constrained, ship-it problems over open-ended research.
* Care about the details that don't show up in a cloud benchmark: cold-start time, power draw, thermals, and memory fragmentation.

**It's Important To Us That You Have**

* Experience delivering production systems on resource-constrained hardware — embedded systems, mobile, edge AI, or small low-power devices.
* Strong proficiency in C, C++, and/or Rust, with experience writing performance-critical code for constrained environments.
* Hands-on experience with model optimization for on-device deployment, including quantization, pruning, knowledge distillation, or architecture-specific compilation.
* Familiarity with edge inference runtimes (e.g., ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, TFLite, ExecuTorch) and/or vendor-specific NPU/DSP toolchains.
* A strong understanding of hardware-software interaction — CPU/GPU/NPU/DSP architectures, memory hierarchies, fixed-point/integer arithmetic, and power management — and how they affect inference performance.
* Experience working close to the metal: bare-metal or RTOS environments (e.g., FreeRTOS, Zephyr), embedded Linux, or microcontroller and edge SoC development.
* Strong communication skills and a builder mindset — you can scope an ambiguous optimization problem, drive it to a measurable result, and explain the tradeoffs clearly.

**It Would Be Great if You Had**

* Experience with real-time audio processing on embedded platforms — DSP pipelines, audio codec optimization, wake-word or always-on listening, or streaming inference on microcontrollers and edge SoCs.
* Depth in ML optimization techniques — custom quantization schemes, mixed-precision inference, or neural architecture search for edge targets.
* Background in hardware evaluation and benchmarking — systematically comparing accelerators, SoCs, or GPUs for specific workload profiles.
* Experience shipping AI features in consumer products at scale, and the instinct for what "production quality" means on a battery-powered device.
* Familiarity with model compilation and optimization toolchains and their tradeoffs across hardware targets.
* Experience with secure, robust on-device deployment practices — code signing, encrypted model storage, and safe update mechanisms.
